summary: Atlas-owned timeblocking calendar application: users create, edit, move, and delete calendar blocks, optionally linked to TaskTracker tasks, persisted in Postgres.

classification.why_application: Owns calendar block domain logic, event lifecycle rules, task-linking semantics, and user-facing CRUD behavior — application-specific, not reusable platform infrastructure.
classification.not_platform: Calendar blocks carry domain meaning (task_block, personal_block, blocker) and enforce application-specific rules (start_at < end_at, task link semantics). This is not reusable generic infrastructure.

consumes: TaskTracker task IDs as opaque foreign references (no join, no ownership)
provides: POST /api/cal/events creates a new CalendarEvent, returns Dataset (single row)
PATCH /api/cal/events/{event_id} partially updates a CalendarEvent, returns Dataset (single row)
DELETE /api/cal/events/{event_id} deletes a CalendarEvent, returns empty Dataset
Invariant: start_at < end_at is enforced by the backend on create and update
Invariant: deleting a CalendarEvent never deletes the linked task
Invariant: updating a CalendarEvent never updates the linked task
invariants: start_at must be strictly before end_at — enforced on create and patch
source_object_type must be 'task' when source_object_id is provided, null otherwise
A CalendarEvent deletion is independent of TaskTracker — the linked task is never modified
PATCH distinguishes field omission from explicit null: omitted fields unchanged, explicit null clears nullable fields (notes, source_object_id, source_object_type)
failure_modes: CALENDAR_EVENT_NOT_FOUND — event_id does not exist, returns 404 ApiError
CALENDAR_VALIDATION_ERROR — start_at >= end_at or source_object fields inconsistent, returns 422 ApiError
CALENDAR_INVALID_PATCH — patch body contains invalid field combination, returns 422 ApiError

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/cal/events
exposed_surfaces.purpose: List all CalendarEvents ordered by start_at ASC. Supports optional query params: start (ISO-8601 datetime, inclusive lower bound) and end (ISO-8601 datetime, exclusive upper bound). Returns Dataset.

params.start: ISO-8601 datetime string, optional, inclusive — filters events where start_at >= start
params.end: ISO-8601 datetime string, optional, exclusive — filters events where start_at < end

exposed_surfaces.default_behavior: No params returns all events ordered start_at ASC
exposed_surfaces.empty_result: Returns Dataset with empty rows array and total=0

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/cal/events
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Create a new CalendarEvent. Returns Dataset (single row) on success.

exposed_surfaces.name: PATCH /api/cal/events/{event_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Partially update a CalendarEvent. Field omission means no change. Explicit null clears nullable fields. Returns Dataset (single row).

patch_semantics.provided_as_null: nullable fields (notes, source_object_id, source_object_type) cleared to NULL

exposed_surfaces.name: DELETE /api/cal/events/{event_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Delete a CalendarEvent by ID. Returns empty Dataset on success, 404 ApiError if not found.

internal_flow.name: request_received
internal_flow.description: FastAPI router receives HTTP request. Path/query/body parameters validated by Pydantic models. Event ID extracted from path for PATCH and DELETE.
outputs: Pydantic-validated request model or 422 validation error

internal_flow.name: business_validation
internal_flow.description: For create and update: verify start_at < end_at. Verify source_object consistency: if source_object_id is provided then source_object_type must be 'task' and vice versa. If validation fails, return 422 ApiError with CALENDAR_VALIDATION_ERROR code.

internal_flow.name: database_operation
internal_flow.description: CalendarEventRepository executes the appropriate SQL via psycopg2 (RealDictCursor): INSERT for create, UPDATE with partial fields for patch (omitted fields excluded from SET clause), DELETE for delete, SELECT for list (with optional start/end filters and ORDER BY start_at ASC).
outputs: CalendarEvent record(s) or not-found signal or DB error

internal_flow.name: response_mapping
internal_flow.description: CalendarEventMapper converts CalendarEvent record(s) to Dataset shape. Meta contains object_type='calendar_event', label='Calendar Events', total=count, page=1, page_size=count, row_actions=['edit','delete']. Schema columns: id, title, start_at, end_at, event_type, source_object_type, source_object_id, notes, created_at, updated_at.

internal_flow.name: response_returned
internal_flow.description: Router returns Dataset as JSON response. On error, returns ApiError envelope.

external_required.name: psycopg2
external_required.role: Postgres driver (RealDictCursor pattern, consistent with all Atlas applications)

external_required.name: @fullcalendar/react
external_required.role: Calendar UI component library for week/day view with drag and resize

external_required.name: @fullcalendar/interaction
external_required.role: FullCalendar drag, resize, and click interaction plugin

forbidden: CalendarConnector — that service is the Google Calendar adapter; this application must NOT call it
Direct task table joins — task data is accessed only by task_id reference, never by joining the tasks table

application_implementer: Implement FastAPI router at backend/routers/calendar.py with four endpoints
Implement CalendarEventRepository with psycopg2 (RealDictCursor): list (with optional start/end filter), get_by_id, create, patch (partial update excluding omitted fields), delete
Implement CalendarEventMapper converting DB rows to Dataset
Implement Pydantic models: CalendarEventCreate, CalendarEventPatch (all fields Optional with sentinel for omit-vs-null), CalendarEventRow
Run database migration 001_calendar_events.sql against atlas DB
Implement conftest.py with atlas_test DB connection and fixture loading
Implement tests/test_calendar.py covering all test spec scenarios
Implement tests/fixtures.sql with at least 3 CalendarEvent fixtures covering: standalone block, task-linked block, personal block
Implement compose entry for atlas-calendar container at port 8023
ui_implementer: Implement src/ShellEntry.tsx: FullCalendar week view as default, day view switch, event rendering, drag-to-move (updates start_at and end_at), resize-to-extend (updates end_at), click-to-open edit modal, time range select to create new event

Implement EventModal component: form for title, start_at, end_at, event_type, source_object_id (text input for task id), notes fields; Save and Delete buttons; validation showing error if start >= end
Implement src/shellConfig.ts registering appId='calendar', basePath='/calendar', mobilePrimaryNav=[{id:'calendar-week', label:'Week', path:'/calendar'}], desktopNav same
Add side-effect import of Calendar shellConfig to 02_Platform/Atlas_Shell/src/shell/main.tsx
Call GET /api/cal/events on mount passing current view's start/end window as query params; re-fetch on view navigation
On drag/resize: call PATCH /api/cal/events/{id} with new start_at/end_at; on failure show inline error
On delete: call DELETE /api/cal/events/{id}; on success remove from calendar
On create: call POST /api/cal/events with form data; on success add to calendar
test_writer: Map test spec scenarios to pytest functions in tests/test_calendar.py
Use fixtures.sql as test data source via conftest truncate-and-reload
reviewer: Verify PATCH null-vs-omit semantics are correctly implemented in the Pydantic patch model
Verify URL prefix /api/cal does not conflict with CalendarConnector's /api/calendar prefix
Verify FullCalendar dependency is added to Atlas Shell package.json, not duplicated per-app
Verify start_at < end_at invariant is enforced in business_validation, not just in the DB constraint

deferred_decisions: Port number for atlas-calendar container — 8023 proposed (8022=StorageTracker, 8024+ unused)
Whether FullCalendar license (open-source v6 MIT) is acceptable — assumed yes for MVP

risks.impact: nginx or API gateway may route /api/calendar/* to the wrong backend. This design uses /api/cal to avoid the conflict but reviewers must verify nginx/proxy config handles both prefixes correctly.

risks.risk: FullCalendar drag/resize events fire onChange with partial objects; implementer must map these carefully to PATCH body
risks.impact: If start_at or end_at is not extracted correctly from FullCalendar event objects, drag/resize will silently corrupt event times

risks.risk: source_object_id references a task that may not exist
risks.impact: No FK constraint is enforced across application boundaries. A stale task_id reference will not cause a DB error but will display a dangling link in the UI. This is acceptable for MVP.

open_questions.question: Should GET /api/cal/events default to returning only the current week's events, or all events? The draft says 'view calendar blocks in week/day view' suggesting a windowed fetch is intended.
open_questions.resolution: Design declares: no params returns all events; UI caller passes start/end params matching the visible FullCalendar window. This satisfies the MVP requirement without inventing a server-side default window.

open_questions.question: Should DELETE return 204 No Content or an empty Dataset?
open_questions.resolution: Draft says 'empty Dataset or 204 for delete'. Design chooses empty Dataset (200) to match the pattern used by other Atlas applications (StorageTracker, TaskTracker) for consistency.
